reviews.one_line_contribution: Re-runs MAGE's coupling effect on an agent benchmark as a crossed optimizer-seed x bank-seed x eval-seed random-effects experiment, so that the amplified variance is attributed to a specific component (the optimizer-by-bank interaction, i.e. the evolved instruction is fit to the bank it was scored against) and the mean gain is re-tested at matched episode budget.
reviews.closest_prior_work: MAGE (arXiv:2607.11944, verified via s2cli: 'when multiple stochastic optimization signals operate within a closed reflective loop, they interact in ways that simultaneously improve performance and amplify variance, behavior that cannot be predicted by analyzing components in isolation'). MAGE does not decompose the variance, does not cost-match and is single-turn, so it does not scoop the decomposition outright, but it does own the phenomenon, the framing, and the key sentence ('cannot be predicted from components in isolation') that the proposal's interaction hypothesis restates in ANOVA vocabulary. The sharper methodological threat is p1 (arXiv:2604.08801, verified): it already partitions the variance a prompt optimizer sees into response stochasticity vs system-prompt quality variance and turns the partition into an actionable method; it is memory-free and single-turn, so the proposal's increment is which factors get crossed, not the idea of decomposing an optimizer's variance. MEMO (arXiv:2603.09022, verified) already links memory-augmented context optimization to run-to-run variance in multi-turn settings with uncertainty-aware selection. Internally, the program's own archived memory_dropout_coadaptation and coadaptation_transplant_ccr already propose the bank-swap diagnostic that is P3 here; averaging the swap over a 3x3 grid and fitting a mixed model to it is an increment on an idea the program already scored at 5.45-5.77.
reviews.strongest_objection: The paper's every deliverable is a variance component estimated from three levels. With o in {1,2,3} and b in {1,2,3}, sigma2_O and sigma2_B each have 2 degrees of freedom and sigma2_OB has 4; a variance estimated on 2-4 df has a bootstrap CI spanning roughly an order of magnitude, so P1 ('sigma2_OB >= sigma2_O + sigma2_B, refuted if below half of it') cannot be adjudicated - the data cannot separate a ratio of 0.5 from a ratio of 2. Worse, sigma2_O and sigma2_B in P1 are imported from the GEPA-only and store-only arms, which are different experiments with different designs, so the comparison mixes estimands. Boundary estimates (sigma2 = 0) are very likely with 9 cell means and three random effects, and the plan's parametric-bootstrap CIs and LRT on the interaction are exactly the procedures known to misbehave at the boundary (an LRT for a variance component needs a mixture-chi2 null, unmentioned). Then item (7) proposes to publish a seed-count design rule derived from these same near-unidentified components - a reporting standard for the field built on the least reliable quantity in the study. Separately, P4 predicts that a 95% CI contains zero, which underpowering guarantees: with a stated MDE of about 4 points, 'no significant advantage' is the default outcome, not a finding, and the plan gives no equivalence margin to distinguish 'the coupled gain is small' from 'we could not see it'.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Invert the compute allocation: make the 8B backbone the primary decomposition with a much wider grid (8x8 optimizer x bank seeds, or at minimum 5x5) so the components have usable df, and demote the 27B run to a sign-confirmation of the interaction rather than the source of the design rule; drop the 120B arm, which is admitted to be underpowered and buys nothing. Replace P4 with a two-one-sided-tests equivalence claim against a pre-registered margin (e.g. 3 points), so a null is earned rather than inherited from low power. Estimate sigma2_O and sigma2_B inside the crossed model rather than importing them from separate arms. Add a size-and-distribution-matched permuted-content bank as the floor for the in-bank minus cross-bank gap, and a same-bank-different-retrieval-seed transplant, so P3 separates 'fit to this bank' from 'fit to this retrieval realization' and from bank-size effects (the disjoint 150-task variant currently confounds content, coverage and size). Finally, anchor the transfer claim by running the same pipeline once on MAGE's own setting (GSM8K-Hard): without it, a P2 failure is indistinguishable from 'our GEPA-plus-store implementation is not MAGE's', and the promised null contribution evaporates.
reviews.missing_baseline: A selection-matched single-channel arm: best-of-9 GEPA-only and best-of-9 store-only, chosen on a validation split, versus the coupled system's validation-selected configuration at the same total episode budget. The coupled design spends its budget on 9 (o,b) draws, and practitioners deploy the selected system, not the cell mean; a higher-variance coupled system can win on selected performance while its mean advantage is exactly zero. P4 therefore tests a quantity nobody reports, and can come out 'CI contains zero' while MAGE's practical claim stands untouched - a reviewer will say the audit misses its own target. (Secondary omission: a winner's-curse-corrected or held-out-reselection version of the same comparison.)
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is unusually good for this program - it names four s2cli queries with IDs, distinguishes channels, and states plainly that WebSearch was refused rather than implying it was run - and I could reproduce its core claims. Verified via s2cli (channel a; WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch blocked, so channel b answered nothing): 2607.11944 MAGE (exists, POCE as described), 2604.08801 p1, 2604.14585 Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip, 2603.09022 MEMO, 2607.14004 Do Agent Optimizers Compound?, 2602.07150 On Randomness in Agentic Evals, 2603.21520 (real, indexed as 'Generalizable Self-Evolving Memory for Automatic Prompt Optimization', consistent with the MemAPO description). Could NOT verify 2508.18749 (the mistake-notebook optimizer): s2cli returns 'not found on S2 or HF'; the proposal leans on it only for the 3-5x compute remark, so nothing central depends on it. My own searches: (1) 'variance decomposition seed crossed random effects prompt optimization memory coupling agent' --recent returned 2609.00621 (Control-Data Flow Separation, stability of prompt optimization in multi-agent pipelines - adjacent stability work, no decomposition), 2606.23664 MAS-PromptBench, 2604.14585, 2604.08801, 2603.18388 VISTA, 2603.09022 - no crossed-seed decomposition; (2) 'co-adaptation between optimized instruction and retrieved memory bank cross-bank transfer agent' returned AdaMEM 2606.05684, Memory-R2 2605.21768, EvolveMem 2605.13941, Memory Transfer Learning 2604.14004, M* 2604.11811 - none swaps banks across independently optimized instructions; (3) 'cost-matched compute-normalized comparison prompt optimization memory agent budget equal tokens' --recent returned budget-routing work (BudgetMem 2602.06025, COMPAS 2608.04336, DUET 2605.08441) but no cost-matched coupled-optimizer audit; (4) 'GEPA reflective prompt evolution experience memory ExpeL ALFWorld combined' returned GEPA itself (2507.19457), Evolving-RL 2605.10663, EDV 2606.24428, Honest Lying 2605.29463 - closest in spirit but none estimates variance components; (5) 'generalizability theory variance components LLM evaluation how many seeds needed reporting standard' --recent returned essentially nothing on-topic (an academic-medicine G-theory tool, 2602.00521 IRT for LLM judges), which is itself informative: the seed-count design rule has no direct competitor. So the collision check earns credit, not novelty: what it establishes is that nobody has decomposed this variance, while MAGE published the phenomenon two months ago and p1 published the decompose-the-optimizer's-variance move five months ago. The novelty score reflects that the unclaimed territory here is a statistical treatment, not a claim.
